introduce: Lie on the floor with your hands behind your ears. Raise your knees and close your right elbow toward your left knee, then close your left elbow toward your right knee. Repeat the exercise.
name: BICYCLE CRUNCHES

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Tighten your abdominals.
Keep your neck relaxed.
Put your hands behind your ears, don't interlock your fingers.
If you can see your elbows, please open your chest.
Exhale when lifting your body and inhale when lowering.
You should feel your abs burning.
You shouldn't feel too much strain in your neck.

introduce: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Put your arms flat at your sides. \n\nThen lift your butt up and down.
name: BUTT BRIDGE

tips.text: This workout should be done on a mat.
Keep your feet around shoulder width apart.
Exhale when lifting your butt, and inhale when lowering it.
This exercise really works on your glutes.
This exercise strengthens your lower back.

introduce: Start on all fours with your knees under your butt and your hands directly under your shoulders. \n\nThen kick one leg back until it is parallel with the ground. Switch to the other side after several sets.
name: GLUTE KICK BACK

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Your toes should point toward the floor.
Keep your lifted leg straight.
Your hands should be directly under your shoulders.
Keep your back flat.
Put your weight on your wrists.
Exhale when lifting your leg, and inhale when lowering it.
You shouldn't feel strain in your back.
This exercise is going to give you a sexy butt.

introduce: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your hands behind your ears. \n\nRaise and twist your torso so your right elbow moves to meet your left knee. Repeat with the other side.
name: CROSSOVER CRUNCH

tips.text: You need to do this exercise on a mat.
Raise your upper body to bring your elbows towards your knees.
Exhale as you slowly raise your upper body, and inhale as you return to the start position.
Your neck shouldn't feel sore.
This exercise targets the obliques and rectus abdominis.
This exercise can tone your abs and treat lower back pain.

introduce:
Start on all fours with your knees under your butt and your hands directly under your shoulders. 

Then take a breath in and make your belly fall down, shoulders roll back and head come up towards the ceiling. 

As you exhale, round your spine toward the ceiling and draw your navel up towards your spine, and drop your head.

Repeat the exercise, matching the movement to your breath.
name: CAT COW POSE

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please make sure your palms are directly under your shoulders.
Please make sure your knees are directly under your hips.
Inhale as your belly falls down, and exhale as your belly curves in.
This exercise works on your spine, back and abs.

introduce:
Start on hands and knees. Put your knees and toes together.

Inhale to lengthen your spine. Exhale, sit your hips back to your heels, arms reaching forward. Rest your forehead, soften your elbows, and lower your chest close to the floor.

Breathe slowly through your nose; with each exhale, release and sink a little deeper.
name: CHILD'S POSE

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please make sure there is enough space between your shoulders and ears.
Please keep your arms stretched forward as you sit back.
This exercise gently stretches your upper back, shoulders, hips and legs.
Inhale to allow your belly to expand into your thighs. Exhale to soften into the pose.

introduce:
Lie on your back with your knees up at a 90 degree angle and your arms lifted towards the ceiling. 

Lower your right leg, and extend your left arm above your head. 

Hold it for one second, then return to the start position and repeat with the other side.
name: DEAD BUG

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please always keep your lower back pressed against the floor.
Please don\'t arch your back.
Too hard? Just extend your arms or legs.
This exercise can help relieve lower back pain.
Inhale when lifting your arm and opposite leg, and exhale when lowering them.

introduce:
Lie on your back with your legs extended. 

Inhale deeply to lengthen your spine. Exhale slowly to lift your right leg and use your left hand to pull your right knee to the left. Extend your right arm to the side, palm down.

Breathe naturally. Hold this position for a few seconds. With each exhale, soften and deepen the twist.
name: SPINE LUMBAR TWIST STRETCH RIGHT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please keep your opposite arm always flat on the floor.
It’s a good exercise to stretch your spine.
Inhale to lengthen the spine. Exhale to deepen the twist and relax.

introduce:
Lie on your back with your legs extended. 

Inhale deeply to lengthen your spine. Exhale slowly to lift your left leg and use your right hand to pull your left knee to the right. Extend your left arm to the side, palm down.

Breathe naturally. Hold this position for a few seconds. With each exhale, soften and deepen the twist.
name: SPINE LUMBAR TWIST STRETCH LEFT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please keep your opposite arm always flat on the floor.
It’s a good exercise to stretch your spine.
Inhale to lengthen the spine. Exhale to deepen the twist and relax.

introduce: Lie on your back with your hands behind your ears and legs raised with knees bent at 90 degrees. \n\nLift your shoulders up off the ground, then slowly return back to the starting position. Repeat the exercise.
name: 90/90 CRUNCH

tips.text: Please do it on a mat.
Please don’t lock your fingers behind your head.
Please keep your neck in a natural position.
Please squeeze your abs when raising up.
Keep your thighs perpendicular to your body and your knees at a 90 degree angle.
Please always keep your lower back on the floor.
Exhale on the way up, and inhale on the way down.
It works on your abs and hip flexors.

introduce:
Lie down on your back with your legs extended. Relax your spine and gently press your lower back into the floor. 

Inhale, lift your knees toward your chest. Exhale, hug your knees gently.

Hold the position without holding your breath. Inhale as you lengthen your spine. Exhale as you soften your shoulders and hips.
name: DOUBLE KNEES TO CHEST

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Hold on your thighs instead if you have knee injuries.
It’s a good exercise to stretch your lower back muscles.
It helps to restore flexibility to your lower back.
Inhale to lengthen your spine. Exhale to relax your shoulders and hips.

introduce:
Lie on your left side with your hand supporting your body. 

Stretch and lift your right hand to make your body form a letter “T”. 

Keep your body straight. Hold this position.

Don't hold your breath. Breathe normally from your abdomen instead of your chest.
name: LEFT SIDE PLANK WITH ARM RAISED

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your body straight.
Please tighten your core.
Breathe naturally.
Please put your hand directly under your shoulder.

introduce:
Lie on your right side with your hand supporting your body. 

Stretch and lift your left hand to make your body form a letter “T”. 

Keep your body straight. Hold this position.

Don't hold your breath. Breathe normally from your abdomen instead of your chest.
name: RIGHT SIDE PLANK WITH ARM RAISED

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your body straight.
Please tighten your core.
Breathe naturally.
Please put your hand directly under your shoulder.

introduce: Lie flat on your back with legs extended wider than hip-width apart, arms relaxed by your sides, palms up. \n\nInhale slowly through your nose, your spine gently lengthening and your body becoming light. Exhale fully, allowing your shoulders, hips, and entire body to melt into the mat, and consciously relax any areas of tightness or tension throughout your body.
name: RELAXATION LYING POSE

tips.text: Close your eyes, relax your arms and legs, relax your face, relax the ankles.
Inhale to lengthen your spine. Exhale to release tension of your body.
Let any weight, any tension relax to the earth, feel the floor below you, supporting you.
Let every part of your body relax and lower to the ground.
Invite rest and peace into your mind, body and soul.

introduce:
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.

Inhale to lengthen the spine. Exhale, shift weight to the right foot, and press the left sole on your inner calf or thigh. Bring your hands to a prayer position at your chest. 

Hold this position with steady breath. With each exhale, relax your shoulders and press your left knee open.
name: TREE POSE RIGHT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep looking ahead.
Extend your spine.
Press your foot against your inner thigh.
Don\'t press your foot on knee joint of standing leg.
Engage your abs to maintain balance instead of ankle.
Inhale to lengthen your spine. Exhale to press your left knee open.
If too easy for you, extend your arms overhead, and keep your elbows straight.
If too hard for you, lower heel to your calf or ankle.
Your neck and shoulders should not feel tense.
This is a good exercise for your core and your lower body.

introduce:
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.

Inhale to lengthen the spine. Exhale, shift weight to the left foot, and press the right sole on your inner calf or thigh. Bring your hands to a prayer position at your chest. 

Hold this position with steady breath. With each exhale, relax your shoulders and press your right knee open.
name: TREE POSE LEFT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep looking ahead.
Extend your spine.
Press your foot against your inner thigh.
Don\'t press your foot on knee joint of standing leg.
Engage your abs to maintain balance instead of ankle.
Inhale to lengthen your spine. Exhale to press your right knee open.
If too easy for you, extend your arms overhead, and keep your elbows straight.
If too hard for you, lower heel to your calf or ankle.
Your neck and shoulders should not feel tense.
This is a good exercise for your core and your lower body.

introduce:
Start in a high plank position. 

Exhale as you squeeze your glutes, bend your left knee towards your chest, and keep your right leg straight. Inhale as you return to the plank position, then switch legs.

Repeat slowly and maintain a slow, controlled pace with steady breath.
name: SLOW MOUNTAIN CLIMBER

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your abs tight.
Keep your spine neutral and stable.
Keep your body straight.
Bring your knees as close to your chest as possible.
Don\'t lift your hips up.
Exhale when you bend your knee, and inhale when you stretch straight.
If this is too hard for you, put your hands on a bench.
This is a great core exercise for working on your abs, glutes and hip flexors.

introduce:
Sit on the floor with knees bent. Hold your shins and draw your knees toward your chest.

Inhale to roll back, keeping your spine rounded. Exhale as you roll forward toward your knees.

Repeat the pose with a steady breathing rhythm.
name: SPINAL ROLLING

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please keep your spine rounded.
Engage your core to keep balance.
Don\'t roll back too far on your neck.
Keep the movement controlled.
Inhale to roll back. Exhale to roll forward.
This exercise can loosen up your spine and relieve your back pain.

introduce:
Start in a kneeling position. Extend your left leg out to the side, keeping the foot flat on the ground. 

Inhale, lift your arms out to the sides at shoulder height, parallel to the floor. Exhale, bend your upper body to the left, bringing your left hand down to rest on your left leg. Reach your right arm over your head, extending it towards the left.

Hold for a few seconds. And lengthen your right side with each inhale and deepen the stretch with each exhale. Inhale to lift your torso back to the starting position, bringing your arms back to shoulder height.
name: GATE POSE LEFT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Inhale to lengthen your right side. Exhale to deepen the stretch.
Don\'t bend too far so that your breathing is inhibited.
Keep your chest facing forward.
This exercise can lengthen and open the side of your body.
This exercise can stretch the inner thigh of the extended leg.

introduce:
Start in a kneeling position. Extend your right leg out to the side, keeping the foot flat on the ground. 

Inhale, lift your arms out to the sides at shoulder height, parallel to the floor. Exhale, bend your upper body to the right, bringing your right hand down to rest on your right leg. Reach your left arm over your head, extending it towards the right.

Hold for a few seconds. And lengthen your left side with each inhale and deepen the stretch with each exhale. Inhale to lift your torso back to the starting position, bringing your arms back to shoulder height.
name: GATE POSE RIGHT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Inhale to lengthen your left side. Exhale to deepen the stretch.
Don't bend too far so that your breathing is inhibited.
Keep your chest facing forward.
This exercise can lengthen and open the side of your body.
This exercise can stretch the inner thigh of the extended leg.

introduce:
Lie on your back with legs extended and arms by your sides. 

Inhale, then lift your upper body and legs off the floor. Exhale as you extend your arms forward and draw your navel in.

Hold this position with steady breath. With each inhale, keep the spine long; with each exhale, engage the core and release tension.
name: LOW BOAT POSE

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Focus all the tension on your core.
Inhale to lengthen your spine, exhale to release tension.
Keep your neck relaxed.
This exercise works your core.

introduce:
Lie on your stomach with your legs extended and your arms by your sides. 

As you inhale, lift your head, chest, arms, and legs off the ground, firming your shoulder blades onto your back. Imagine someone grasping your hands, gently pulling you back, to come up higher.

Hold this position. Use the inhale to support the lift of your head, chest, arms, and legs.
name: LOCUST POSE

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your pelvis on the floor when lifting your legs.
Inhale to lift higher. Exhale to release your tension.
This exercise tones your buttocks and strengthens your back muscles.

introduce:
Start in a kneeling position with your thighs vertical to the floor. Extend your right leg out to the side with the foot flat on the floor.

Put your left hand on the floor, directly under your shoulder. Inhale the right arm up and over the head with the palm facing the floor.

Hold this position. Inhale to extend and open your torso, exhale to relax and deepen the stretch along your side.
name: HALF CIRCLE POSE LEFT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your pelvis neutral and stable.
Keep your chest facing forward.
Draw your shoulders away from your ears.
This exercise stretches the side of your body.
This exercise opens your chest and hips.
Inhale to extend your body. Exhale to relax and deepen the stretch of your side.

introduce:
Start in a kneeling position with your thighs vertical to the floor. Extend your left leg out to the side with the foot flat on the floor.

Put your right hand on the floor, directly under your shoulder. Inhale the left arm up and over the head with the palm facing the floor.

Hold this position. Inhale to extend and open your torso, exhale to relax and deepen the stretch along your side.
name: HALF CIRCLE POSE RIGHT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your pelvis neutral and stable.
Keep your chest facing forward.
Draw your shoulders away from your ears.
This exercise stretches the side of your body.
This exercise opens your chest and hips.
Inhale to extend your body. Exhale to relax and deepen the stretch of your side.

introduce:
Stand with your feet hip-width apart, draw your belly in, and roll your shoulders back and down.

Inhale and raise your arms overhead and lengthen your spine. Exhale and hinge forward from your hips, keeping your spine long. Place your hands on your shins.

Hold the position with slow, deep breaths through your nose. Inhale to extend the spine, exhale to relax and release deeper into the fold.
name: HALF FORWARD BEND

tips.text: Bend from your hips instead of your waist.
Keep your legs straight but don\'t lock your knees.
Focus on keeping your back flat and lengthening your spine.
Inhale to extend the spine, exhale to release deeper into the fold.
This exercise stretches your hamstrings.
This exercise strengthens your back.

introduce:
Lay prone with your hands under your shoulders and the tops of your feet on the floor. 

Inhale as you press through your hands firmly into the floor. Straighten your arms and lift your chest. Slightly lift your thighs off the ground. Gaze forward or slightly upward.

Hold the position with deep and steady breath. Inhale to expand your chest and lengthen your spine, exhale to soften your shoulders, relax your neck, and keep your arms and core stable.
name: UPWARD FACING DOG

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Rotate your shoulders back and down.
Keep your legs engaged, don\'t slouch them on the floor.
Keep your neck natural, don\'t strain your neck.
This exercise stretches your chest, abdomen, and spine.
This exercise can firm your buttocks and thighs.
Inhale to lift your chest. Exhale to soften your shoulders.

introduce: Start on all fours. Exhale as you lift your hips into an inverted ‘V’ shape, and lengthen your spine.\n\nAlternately lift and lower your heels with steady breath.
name: WALK THE DOG

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Relax your neck.
Keep a steady and even breathing rhythm without holding your breath.
Notice the elongation from your fingertips to your sit bone.
Draw your shoulders away from your ears.
Please press all areas of the palms equally on the floor.
This exercise stretches your shoulders, hamstrings, calves, and arches.

introduce:
Lie on your back and inhale. Exhale to draw your knees toward your chest, separate the knees, and raise the feet so the soles of the feet are toward the ceiling.

Inhale, grab the inside of your feet. Exhale, gently sink the shoulders and tailbone toward the floor.

Hold the position. Inhale to lengthen the spine, exhale to soften your hips and lower back into the mat.
name: HAPPY BABY POSE

tips.text: Please do this on the mat.
Inhale to lengthen the spine. Exhale to soften your hips and lower back.
Keep your head on the mat to avoid neck strain.
This exercise can help relieve your lower back pain.
This exercise stretches your inner thighs, hamstrings, groin, and spine.

introduce:
Start on all fours with your knees under your butt and your hands directly under your shoulders. 

Tuck your toes, straighten your legs and lift your hips up into an upside down 'V' shape. 

Transfer your weight back to your legs. Press your heels on the mat. Grab your right ankle with your left hand. 

Hold for a moment, then switch to the other side.
name: REVOLVED DOWNWARD FACING DOG

tips.text: Please prepare a mat.
Breathe regularly.
This exercise stretches your full body.

introduce: Stand upright with your weight on your left foot. Bend your right knee and use your right hand to grab your toes with your thumb up. \n\nReach your right knee backward and your left arm forward. Fix your eyes in front of you. Hold this position.
name: LORD OF THE DANCE LEFT

tips.text: If it's difficult to maintain balance, you can use your hand to hold a wall.
Slightly bend the knee of your standing leg.
This pose opens your hip flexors and shoulders.
This pose helps improve your balance and concentration.

introduce: Stand upright with your weight on your right foot. Bend your left knee and use your left hand to grab your toes with your thumb up. \n\nReach your left knee backward and your right arm forward. Fix your eyes in front of you. Hold this position.
name: LORD OF THE DANCE RIGHT

tips.text: If it's difficult to maintain balance, you can use your hand to hold a wall.
Slightly bend the knee of your standing leg.
This pose opens your hip flexors and shoulders.
This pose helps improve your balance and concentration.

introduce:
Stand upright with your feet together. 

Inhale, raise your arms overhead with your palms facing each other. Exhale, gently bend backward, pushing your pelvis forward. Keep your arms in line with your ears and your chest lifted. 

Hold the position. Inhale as you lengthen your spine and lift your chest higher. Exhale to bend deeper into the pose.
name: STANDING BACKBEND

tips.text: Keep your core tight and spine neutral.
Keep your tailbone tucked down.
Inhale to lengthen your spine. Exhale to deepen the stretch.
This pose stretches your chest, shoulders and upper abdomen.
This pose elongates your spine and improves your posture.
